title: Shinnecock Presbyterian Church
summary: The Shinnecock Presbyterian church on the Shinnecock Indian Reservation has been described as “the oldest, ongoing Native American church in America.” A regular schedule of tribal gatherings occur here, including the annual June Meeting, Indian Thanksgiving dinner and harvest celebrations. For many years, tribal meetings and Tribal Council elections were held in the Parish Hall before taking place in the Tribal Community Center. why_this_matters: Recognized as the oldest ongoing Native American church in the country, the Shinnecock Presbyterian Church actively continues to host both traditional harvest celebrations and tribal council elections. The endurance of this vital community center illustrates how Indigenous peoples strategically adapted Christian institutions to protect their sovereignty and sustain their own deeply rooted communal bonds.
introduction_content:
Community Anchor

Shinnecock Presbyterian Church is an important place for understanding community continuity, Christian worship, education, and local leadership within Shinnecock history. The church also connects to public gatherings and early powwows that supported community institutions.

The mapped place focuses on the church itself and does not identify nearby burial or sensitive community spaces.

Related Biography

Rev. Paul Cuffee's life connects this site to a wider Native Long Island history of Shinnecock, Unkechaug, Montaukett, and other community relationships through churches, preaching circuits, and seasonal gatherings. See the Rev. Paul Cuffee biography for person-focused context.
